Codex Token Usage: Read Local Counters Without Double Counting

To inspect Codex usage, start with the product’s own status and usage views. To check a local JSONL file, keep cumulative snapshots separate from individual response records. The reader below deduplicates supported response IDs and exports counters only. A local token count does not establish your remaining plan allowance or bill.

Read a Codex JSONL file locally

Try the synthetic example first. Then choose one uncompressed UTF-8 rollout JSONL file from your own Codex installation, or a counter-only excerpt. The browser reads it in this tab; this tool does not upload the file or save it to browser storage. The download omits prompts, paths, file names, model labels, IDs, timestamps and rate-limit data.

Up to 20,000 lines and 256 KiB characters per line. Decompress archives on your computer first. A counter-only excerpt may produce a partial result.

Choose a file or try the example. No real conversation is needed.

The summary covers readable records in the selected file. Missing counters remain Unknown. A successful import means the reader finished; it does not mean the file is complete or the counters are a provider-certified usage statement. Why 4,300 and 1,300 can both appear

Our hand-authored example contains two responses. The first reports 1,000 input tokens, including 200 cached, plus 100 output tokens. The second reports 3,000 input, including 2,800 cached, plus 200 output. It also repeats the first response and its snapshot once to exercise deduplication.

Synthetic arithmetic, not measured model usage
CounterFirst responseSecond responseCombined
Input, including cached1,0003,0004,000
Cached input detail2002,8003,000
Output100200300
Reported total1,1003,2004,300
Uncached input + output9004001,300

Reported total: 4,000 input + 300 output = 4,300.

CLI-style blended total: (4,000 input − 3,000 cached input) + 300 output = 1,300.

In the checked Codex source, the token-usage display uses a blended total of non-cached input plus output, with cached input shown separately. It is not the same field as total_tokens. Reasoning output is detail within output; adding it again would inflate the count. The reader retains cache-write detail when present, without adding it to input again. See the pinned TokenUsage implementation.

Adding every cumulative snapshot is another error. This fixture contains snapshots of 1,100, 1,100 and 4,300. Their sum is 6,500, but the latest reported snapshot is 4,300. The reader shows the latest snapshot alongside the unique-response sum; it never adds those views together.

Which records count?

Reader rules for the checked rollout schema
RecordReader behaviorLimit
event_msg → token_count → info.total_token_usageShow the last valid snapshot in file order. Count repeated snapshots separately from distinct updates.A snapshot is a reported state, not another response to add.
token_usage_record → payload.usageSum unique thread + response IDs within scope.Do not add turn_token_usage or thread_token_usage again.
info: null or absentCount an update without usage; leave earlier counters intact.A rate-only update does not mean zero tokens.
Messages, tool output and nested textIgnore content.Text that merely resembles counter JSON is not usage evidence.

The rollout wire format puts the record type beside its payload. The persistence policy includes both usage-event and response-record forms. Their coexistence does not make them independent charges.

Forks and repeated headers: the first session header, when usable, sets the response-record thread scope. Later headers may be inherited history; they do not switch the scope. Records from other thread IDs are excluded and counted. Without a canonical header, more than one observed thread suppresses the sum. A single observed thread can be summed with a scope warning. Snapshots remain file observations and are not certified child-only totals.

Conflicts and unusual counters: a repeated response ID with different counters suppresses the response sum. Negative, fractional, unsafe or missing required values are skipped with a warning. A decreasing snapshot or a total different from input + output is shown with a warning. The checked source can fill counters to a context-window estimate, so an arithmetic mismatch alone does not establish a producer bug. Malformed lines also make the result partial.

Token counters, plan limits and bills answer different questions

Choose the measurement that answers your question
Your questionWhere to check
What configuration and session usage does Codex show?Use /status. The current command reference also documents /usage activity views; availability depends on the client, version and authentication.
What did this local file report?Use this reader, with its selected-file and schema limits.
How much subscription allowance remains?Use the product’s current usage/limits view for your account. Local token sums are not remaining allowance.
What did API use cost?Use the billing records for the API account and the applicable model rates. A ChatGPT subscription and API-key billing are separate.

OpenAI’s current CLI command reference explains the product views. Its Codex pricing documentation separates API-key billing from plan usage. The reader does not convert local tokens into dollars, credits, remaining messages or context remaining. It also cannot see activity that was not recorded in your chosen file.

Tests, scope and sources

We checked the locally installed codex-cli 0.167.0 version and read the matching official release source at commit 086ccc8. We did not inspect a private session to build this guide. The downloadable fixture is hand-authored and counter-shaped; it is not a real conversation, a replayable Codex session or an account-billing experiment.

The executable checks cover duplicate snapshots and responses, conflicting IDs, copied fork headers, mixed unscoped threads, counter decreases, context-fill shaped totals, rate-only updates, truncated lines, invalid numbers, integer overflow, unknown fields, file bounds and removal of private fields from exports and analytics. These checks establish the reader’s handling of those cases; they do not establish full compatibility with every log version.

Download the source and fixture method. Use the official 0.167.0 release and pinned source links above to audit the schema. Recheck the installed client when your file reports another version.

For coding-tool selection, use the Claude Code / Cursor same-task trial kit. For moving an API client to a local model, see the Ollama / LM Studio same-file exercise. Neither a higher token count nor a lower local counter proves better code or a cheaper subscription.
